{{short description|Intermittent increases and decreases in network activity}}
In [[temporal network]]s, '''burstiness''' is the intermittent increases and decreases in activity or [[frequency]] of an event.<ref name="Lambiotte">Lambiotte, R. (2013.) "Burstiness and Spreading on Temporal Networks", University of Namur.</ref><ref>Neuts, M. F. (1993.) "The Burstiness of Point Processes", ''Commun. Statist.—Stochastic Models'', 9(3):445–66.</ref>
One measure of burstiness is the [[Fano factor]]—a ratio between the [[variance]] and [[mean]] of counts.

Burstiness is observable in natural phenomena, such as [[natural disaster]]s, or other phenomena, such as [[computer network|network]]/[[data]]/[[email]] network traffic<ref>D'Auria, B. and Resnick, S. I. (2006.) "Data network models of burstiness", ''Adv. in Appl. Probab.'', 38(2):373–404.</ref><ref>Ying, Y.; Mazumdar, R.; Rosenberg, C.; Guillemin, F. (2005.) "The Burstiness Behavior of Regulated Flows in Networks", ''Proceedings of the 4th IFIP-TC6 International Conference on Networking Technologies, Services, and Protocols, Performance ofo Computer and Communication Networks, Mobile and Wireless Communication Systems'', 3462:918–29.</ref> or [[Traffic flow|vehicular traffic]].<ref>Jagerman, D. L. and Melamed, B. (1994.) "Burstiness Descriptors of Traffic Streams: Indices of Dispersion and Peakedness", ''Proceedings of the 1994 Conference on Information Sciences and Systems'', 1:24–8.</ref> Burstiness is, in part, due to changes in the [[probability distribution]] of inter-event times.<ref>Goh, K.-I. and Barabasi, A.-L. (2006.) [https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0610233 "Burstiness and Memory in Complex Systems"], ''Physics Data''.</ref> Distributions of bursty processes or events are characterised by [[Fat-tailed distribution|heavy, or fat, tails]].<ref name="Lambiotte"/>

Burstiness of inter-contact time between nodes in a [[time-varying network]] can decidedly slow spreading processes over the network. This is of great interest for studying the spread of information and disease. <ref> P. Holme, J. Saramäki (2012) "Temporal Networks", [[Physics Reports]] 519: 118–120 {{doi|10.1016/j.physrep.2012.03.001}}</ref>

== Burstiness score ==

One relatively simple measure of burstiness is burstiness score. The burstiness score of a subset <math>t</math> of time period <math>T</math> relative to an event <math>e</math> is a measure of how often <math>e</math> appears in <math>t</math> compared to its occurrences in <math>T</math>. It is defined by

: <math>\mathrm{Burst}(e, t) = \left (\frac{E_t}{E} - \frac{1}{T}\right ) </math>

Where <math>E_t</math> is the total number of occurrences of event <math>e</math> in subset   <math>t</math> and <math>E</math> is the total number of occurrences of <math>e</math> in <math>T</math>.

Burstiness score can be used to determine if <math>t</math> is a "bursty period" relative to <math>e</math>. A positive score says that <math>e</math> occurs more often during subset <math>t</math> than over total time <math>T</math>, making <math>t</math> a bursty period. A negative score implies otherwise. <ref> A. Hoonlor et al. (2013). "[http://www.cs.rpi.edu/research/pdf/12-03.pdf An Evolution of Computer Science Research]", ''Communications of the ACM'', 56(10):79 </ref>
